reply_text:
It didn't come from you, and the run records show it has been this way for as long as there are certificates to read. I counted the policy set in every recorded selection and added it to the incident (commit `8096a513a`).

**What the records show** (30 of the 76 run records carry a selection certificate):

- **Every run that selected a target and dispatched an author had exactly one candidate and one policy.** That covers M-autoclock-in, M-aif-policy-conditioned-eig on 29 September, M-self-documenting-stack three times, and M-descriptive-essay-of-the-stack twice.
- **The largest policy set ever recorded is 24 policies over 21 targets**, in three runs on 21 September. None of those selected anything.
- **From 22 September on, it is 1, 2 or 3 in every record.**
- **The patterns came from five hand-written files** in `resources/wm/cascade-sources/`, plus the per-target interpretation answers from today. At no point was a policy set derived from the pattern library for the problem at hand.

So the scoring is real, and what it has been fed is a hand-written menu. Every selection the machine has made that led to work was a choice among one. That is a facade in the sense you mean: the grounded change I reported this morning as click 13's success was the machine "choosing" the only thing on its list.

**Who introduced it.** Git can't attribute it to an agent: the commits carry your git identity, and agent trailers only exist from today. The commit messages name two steps: claude-20's resolutions in the spec on 15 September, and the "hand-admitted" first target on 17 September. I took the machine over on 28 September and carried on repairing it without counting what it was choosing among.

**What I've added to the incident's closing conditions.** Beyond the code repair, the Lean has to state where the policy set comes from, so that a hand-fed menu can't satisfy it. The negative control is a menu that isn't the result of construction over the library for the problem; it must fail conformance. That work belongs to the controller and selection owners together.

codex-4's job on the code side is running (`invoke-1790754890969-28889-921071df`, parked): the two failing negative tests, and the ordered changes that put the library slice in the constructor's pool with interpretation after selection.
